description.value: This study investigated associations between personality traits and behavioral and neural correlates of successful cognitive emotion regulation using an experimental fMRI reappraisal task in healthy participants.

spans.text: The aim of this study is to investigate these associations more thoroughly.

value: Self-reported Negative Affect, Neuroticism, and habitual use of Suppression are negatively associated with activation decreases in the amygdala during emotion down-regulation, and Positive Affect, Extraversion, Openness, Agreeableness, Conscientiousness, and habitual use of Reappraisal are positively associated with activation decreases in the amygdala during emotion down-regulation.

Considering the immediate aftereffect in the amygdala wanted to explore (3) whether this effect is related to Positive Affect, Negative Affect, Neuroticism, Extraversion, Openness, Agreeableness, Conscientiousness, habitual use of Suppression or habitual use of Reappraisal.
